reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage BUSD as an income opportunity, citing six-figure earnings within short periods and encouraging viewers to sign up, join a team, and invest a one-time amount in a digital asset. It describes recruiting people and building teams as ways to earn returns. The speaker acknowledges effort and uncertainty and advises due diligence, but the available video evidence still describes a direct promotion of a recruitment-based, contribution-linked return opportunity.

opening.argument: The presentation repeatedly rejects the idea of effortless or guaranteed money. It warns viewers about people who promise outcomes without achievement, says the opportunity is not a quick-money scheme, acknowledges that spillover may never arrive, and tells viewers to gain knowledge and save money before joining. That is risk disclosure and due-diligence advice, not a deceptive assurance that everyone will profit.

citations.quote: Else! You will fall into the hands of scammers and the hands of people who will promise you heaven and earth without you achieving anything.

you may be in facage for one month, two two months three months even one year without getting a spillover
find knowledge first and save your money

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes recruitment and contributions, but those excerpts do not establish that the speaker concealed risk or promised an inevitable return. The presentation explicitly says that results require effort, that spillover is uncertain, and that viewers should save their money and investigate first. Those qualifications materially change the message from a guaranteed-income pitch to a conditional business discussion.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings do not neutralize the central promotion. The speaker still says the system can produce substantial income and directs viewers toward joining. Saying that success requires effort describes the conditions for pursuing the opportunity; it does not retract the earnings pitch or make the recruitment-linked structure ordinary. A disclaimer alongside solicitation remains solicitation.

opening.argument: The video is structured as an explanatory lesson: it introduces five reasons participants may fail, defines what the speaker says a smart contract is, and explains knowledge, expectations, strategy, team activity, and habits. The slide sequence visibly presents a checklist of reasons for failure, while the narration repeatedly tells viewers to study the system and understand it before committing. Its primary format is instruction about how the model is said to operate, not proof that a transaction or payment occurred.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the format educational does not answer what it teaches. The lesson explains how to recruit, build teams, and obtain rewards from other participants, then offers access to the speaker's marketing funnel. The instructional framing therefore functions as guidance for entering and expanding the promoted opportunity, rather than neutral technology education.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The checklist and explanations do not merely describe software. They teach viewers how to participate in a program where contributions go to others and rewards depend on other people's efforts. The speaker also ends by inviting viewers to connect and sign up. Educational language cannot erase that the subject matter and requested next step are participation in the promoted scheme.

opening.argument: The available evidence does not establish that any viewer paid, that the speaker received money, or that a promised return was actually delivered. The narration presents conditional participation and repeatedly says that success depends on work, strategy, team activity, and expectations. It also concedes that someone can receive no spillover for a year. Thus, the record shows a business or referral explanation, but not a completed scam transaction or a guaranteed payout.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution need not prove that a viewer completed payment or received a payout to identify the content's nature. The speaker describes contribution-linked rewards, downlines, and recruiting people, then promotes access to a team and funnel. Those are not ordinary retail facts merely because the video also discusses effort and uncertainty.

citations.quote: as 12 digital assets which you have to contribute to each of this digital asset as you contribute goes to some persons indirectly

have access to once you join our team

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a completed transaction is not decisive because the relevant conduct is promotion and instruction. The speaker explicitly describes a one-time contribution, says participants are remunerated through others' fundraising, and urges viewers to sign up. Describing uncertainty about spillover does not remove the recruitment-dependent return mechanism; it only qualifies its timing.
